Hi Stephanie —

We started seeing severe latency and occasional dropped messages on our live chat at about 17:40 PST. Users on our highest-traffic storefronts are seeing very slow responses (chat bubbles loading for multiple seconds) and a few timeouts. Our monitoring shows p95 jumping from ~220ms to ~760ms and p99 to ~2.8s during the peak 17:45-18:00 window. Error rate for SSE connections spiked to ~2.1% (mostly 502/504).

This is impacting checkout flows tied to chat suggestions — we already took down non-critical widgets but impact remains. Can you escalate? We need an incident owner and a mitigation path (fallbacks, routing, or temporary capacity).

Attached is a short perf snapshot from our side and a link to our support ticket: hubspot FT-3492.

—Miguel

From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 18:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nightfall stream spike - p95/p99 regression (customer escalation)

Quick summary from triage (observed 18:10):
- Confirmed p95 jump 220ms -> 740ms, p99 520ms -> 2.8s for SSE endpoint /v1/stream/chat (customer-key FT-3492).
- Error rate rise to ~2.1% driven by WebSocket dropouts and some upstream 502s from an inference worker pool.
- Recent change: a runtime kernel update (deployed 2026-12-07 04:00 UTC) that changed KV-cache eviction heuristics for long-context streams. Canary looked fine for short sessions but not for long-tail session retention.
- During the peak window we see increased sequence length distribution (avg context tokens +22%), which amplifies the eviction behavior and causes increased compute per token on affected workers.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
1) Route FastRetail to older model variant (smaller context handling) — decreased p99 to ~1.1s in controlled test but some quality loss.
2) Scoped rollback on the kernel change to a subset of worker pools — rollback in progress but takes ~12-20m per pool to drain.
3) Capacity burst request to Dedicated pools (if customer is on Hosted we can temporarily move traffic to spare dedicated capacity) — request made to autoscaler.

Requesting: Marcus to authorize expedited rollback across remaining pools and confirm any domino risk. Also request exec visibility if rollback/credits will be needed for SLA.

-David
David Kim
SRE On-Call, Redwood Inference

Laura — please prep an external customer note: what we saw, immediate mitigations, ETA for next update (30m). Steph — loop in Sales leadership if customer requests credits.

-Marcus

Morning Miguel — final update and next steps:

Post-rollback status (completed 02:20 UTC):
- p95 returned to ~240ms (near baseline), p99 stabilized ~820ms during the following evening peak. Error rate returned to <0.2%.
- Root cause: the new KV-cache eviction heuristic increased per-token compute for long-context streams at scale when average context length rose by ~22% in the peak window. The kernel change will be reverted pending a follow-up patch to handle long-tail retention gracefully.

Customer impact & remediation:
- We will provide a root cause report and planned fix timeline within 48 hours.
- As a goodwill gesture for the SLA blip, I'm opening a credit request (FT-3492) for review; Sales leadership will finalize credit amount.
- We recommend FastRetail pin VIP storefronts to a Dedicated pool if you want guaranteed steady p99 during future promotional peaks — happy to set up a call to review Dedicated options and cost/benefit.

Attachments: perf-snapshot-1200-2026-12-08.pdf (customer-provided), hubspot-FT-3492.link

Thanks for your collaboration and patience — apologies for the disruption.

—Steph
